answer: One agent files one cedar deed on the reef board, locking a 70-credit bond, sealed by an onyx key binding key to boundary. The board publishes the deed with its map; an auditor recomputes the boundary, and a mismatch or reused seal burns the bond. Fees follow the queue: the first deed pays 34, the kth pays 34+5(k-1), the 1000th pays 5029, so 1000 fake deeds pay 2,531,500 plus 70,000 in bonds, unshared across deeds. A rented-deed ring fails: a borrowed onyx seal carries the wrong key, so both bonds burn. An honest filer pays 34 once and reclaims the bond after a clean epoch.
